blocks.text: HANGS Construction Services LLC
Client tax questionnaire
Demonstration document. Not for filing or payment.
Year July 1, 2025 to June 30, 2026 (2025 Form 1120).
Date: November 3, 2026. Completed by Morgan Lee for HANGS Construction Services LLC; sent by email to Tax Preparation. Not signed.

Client note: these answers are our own statements, not verified facts. The trial balance behind them is unapproved, and any document described as still being signed or not yet found should be treated as missing.
1. Legal name; any name change?
Answer: HANGS Construction Services LLC. No change.
2. EIN.
Answer: 00-1234567 (demonstration; the 00 prefix is never issued).
3. Address and phone; any change?
Answer: 1200 Example Road, Anytown, WA 00000; 000-555-0100. Unchanged since formation.
4. State and form of organization; entity elections?

Answer: Washington limited liability company; certificate of formation filed June 30, 2023, effective July 1, 2023; Form 8832 election to be taxed as a C corporation from that date; two shareholders, a board of directors and officers.
5. Date business started.
Answer: July 1, 2023: initial cash contributions made and pre-construction work (estimating, permits) began. The first contract was signed in July 2024; nothing was in progress at June 30, 2024.
6. Tax year history.
Answer: June 30 since formation. First return July 1, 2023 to June 30, 2024 (initial); June 30, 2025 return filed. No Form 8716, Form 1128 or section 444 election ever.
7. Business.

Answer: We are a commercial general contractor in Anytown, Washington: we build single-story commercial and light industrial buildings for unrelated owners under fixed-price contracts, with subcontractors; four projects so far. No development, leasing, employees or other income.
8. How is contract revenue billed?

Answer: Owners pay each progress billing within days of the milestone it covers; 104 milestone billings collected at $31,500 each, all cash, last in May 2026. No contract was open at July 1, 2025 or at June 30, 2026; no retainage is withheld; no deferred payment terms.
9. Contract work in progress or unbilled costs at either year end?
Answer: None at either date. Every project started this year was completed and billed by May 2026; June 2026 costs are completion, punch-list and close-out costs on completed projects.
10. Accounting method; statements; method changes.

Answer: Accrual, books and returns. Internal unaudited statements; no applicable financial statement. No Form 3115 ever. We have never capitalized section 263A costs or kept an inventory; construction cost is cost of revenue when each milestone is billed, as on the June 30, 2025 return.
11. Construction contract costs $2,888,500.

Answer: Subcontractor progress payments $2,852,000 (site costs run through the same draw account, not separated); accrued Tallow Creek Framing TCF-2764 $9,400; Harbor Field Counsel HFC-26-0142, Project 4 close-out legal, $18,500 paid June 18, 2026; warranty provision $7,500; completion provision $1,100. Land, materials and labor cannot be split.
12. Estimating and bid costs $143,000.
Answer: Twenty-two payments of $6,500 to Alder and Finch Estimating, the unrelated estimating firm, for estimating fees. Nothing else.
13. Warranty reserve.

Answer: One-year contractual warranty on each completed project. Opening $11,600 covered prior-year projects; six $700 claims ($4,200) went to repair subcontractors for repair work on them, none settled in cash with owners. The $7,500 at June 30, 2026 is our estimate for this year's projects. Post-year-end work not yet summarized.
14. Cost-to-complete reserve.

Answer: Opening $700: punch-list work on prior-year projects by a subcontractor, paid September 30, 2025. The $1,100 at June 30, 2026: estimated punch-list work on projects completed May 2026, on the projects themselves. No obligation for site improvements; owners supplied finished sites.
15. June 30, 2025 return: reserves and organization cost.

Answer: It added back all $12,300 of reserves and deducted none; no recurring item exception or alternative cost method. Its Schedule M-1 showed an organization cost reversal of $480.00 against the $480.33 deducted on the first return; the $0.33 is unexplained. Keep it open; do not plug.
16. Organization costs.
Answer: $480.33 total (Washington filing fee and legal), paid July 2023, deducted in full on the June 30, 2024 return. Nothing capitalized or amortized; no election to capitalize.
17. Accounts payable.

Answer: June 30, 2025: $12,700, Tallow Creek Framing TCF-2291, deducted on that year's return, paid August 12, 2025. June 30, 2026: $9,400, Tallow Creek Framing TCF-2764, framing completion finished June 2026. No related-party payees.
18. Debt and interest.
Answer: Never borrowed; no shareholder loans; no debt canceled or modified; no interest expense or income.
19. Shareholders, percentages, agreement.

Answer: Since July 1, 2023, unchanged: HANGS Holdings Inc, shareholder, 99.9%; HANGS Founders Inc, shareholder, 0.1%; one class of shares, as on earlier returns. The signed agreement is still being circulated; treat the percentages as draft. No guarantees, preferred shares or special dividend rights; cash contributions only; no shares ever sold or exchanged.
20. HANGS Holdings Inc.

Answer: Washington corporation incorporated June 15, 2023; shareholders Celeste Whitford (60%) and Riley Tanaka (40%); IRS acceptance of its EIN on file. EIN 00-3456789 (demonstration); same address as HANGS. Domestic C corporation, June 30 year, Forms 1120 filed since the short year ended June 30, 2023; no S election. Holds only its HANGS shares; no receipts; never required to file Schedule M-3.
21. HANGS Founders Inc.

Answer: Washington corporation incorporated June 15, 2023; sole shareholder Celeste Whitford. EIN 00-2345678 (demonstration); same address. Domestic C corporation, June 30 year, Forms 1120 filed for the same periods; no S election. Holds only its one HANGS founder share; no receipts; never required to file Schedule M-3. President Celeste Whitford is authorized by its bylaws and Washington law to sign for it.
22. Morgan Lee.

Answer: U.S. citizen; SSN 000-00-1234 (demonstration; area 000 is never issued); 1200 Example Road, Anytown, WA 00000; U.S. phone 000-555-0100. No other trade or business; no other entity with gross receipts.
23. Officer compensation and payroll.
Answer: None: no officer or shareholder paid for services; no officer compensation, employees, payroll, Forms W-2 or benefit plans.
24. Dividends.
Answer: Cash on June 30, 2026: $239,760 to HANGS Holdings Inc, $240 to HANGS Founders Inc. No earlier draws, no property. Signed dividend authorization still being collected.
25. Contributions and equity.
Answer: No contributions this year. Book equity $0 at June 30, 2025, $4,500 at June 30, 2026. Tax-basis equity by shareholder at June 30, 2025: $12,287.37 (Holdings Inc), $12.30 (Founders Inc).
26. Trial balance final?
Answer: No; the export is still marked unapproved.
27. Foreign matters; digital assets.

Answer: None: no foreign accounts (2025), trusts, shareholders, operations, payees, Forms 1042/1042-S, specified foreign financial assets or entity interests; no digital assets received, held or sold in 2025.
28. Other entities, elections, transactions.

Answer: HANGS owns no stock or entity interest; is not publicly traded; shares were never offered publicly or in a registered offering. No reportable transaction, like-kind exchange, opportunity fund, foreign acquisition, stock repurchase, 163(j) election or hybrid arrangement. Purpose: commercial construction contracting only.
29. Information returns.

Answer: For 2024 payments: seven Forms 1099-NEC (six subcontractors and the estimating firm, none incorporated), due January 31, 2025, filed January 2025. For 2025 payments: Forms 1099-NEC filed January 2026. The only other return required in calendar 2025 was the June 30, 2025 Form 1120. No Forms W-2, 941, 940 or excise returns.
30. Centralized audit regime.
Answer: Not applicable to a C corporation. Tax contact Jordan Hale, Chief Financial Officer; designated individual Morgan Lee, Controller; both at the address and phone in answer 3.
31. Signer; may the IRS discuss the return with the preparer?
Answer: Celeste Whitford, President & CEO, an officer of the company. Yes.
32. Extension.
Answer: Form 7004 filed September 9, 2026 through our accounting software; acknowledgment not yet located; no disallowance notice.
33. Business continuing?
Answer: Yes; Project 5 is planned for the year ending June 30, 2027. Not winding up; not a final return.
34. Expense support.
Answer: Only HFC-26-0142 so far; support for the 920 progress payments, 22 bid fees and six warranty claims is not yet assembled.
35. Where is the business carried on? State information?
Answer: All projects, construction and revenue are in Washington. No state or local tax information supplied.
36. Book classification of the reserves.
Answer: Both current liabilities; work expected within twelve months.
37. Whole dollars or cents?
Answer: No preference; please decide.
38. Prior-year figures.
Answer: Year ended June 30, 2025: contract revenue $2,840,000; book income $70,000; taxable income per return $82,780. Year ended June 30, 2024: no income; one $480.33 organization cost deduction.
39. Were losses ever carried forward?

Answer: Only the $480.33 loss for the year ended June 30, 2024, carried forward by the company (shareholders 99.9% Holdings Inc and 0.1% Founders Inc). The years ended June 30, 2025 and 2026 had income and no loss.
40. Related-party dealings.
Answer: None other than the dividends in answer 24.
End of questionnaire. No signature.
